title: How big are the square left and the square from the corners?
description: A square card with sides of four centimetres has its four corners cut off, each cut joining the midpoints of two neighbouring sides. The video finds the area of the square left and of the square the corners make. Keeko's doubt is that the square left has an area of four square centimetres.
teaching_notes: One idea: the four corner triangles fit together into a square and cover exactly half of the card. Watch for students who take the slanting cut as two centimetres, half a side.

source: A square has side 4 cm. Its corners are cut off from midpoin
video_script.why: The child imagines cutting and refitting the pieces, as the book asks, and checks the picture with areas.
video_script.substitution: Find the area of the whole square, find the four corners together, then take them away.
video_script.anchor: an imagined square with its four corners cut off, from the lesson of the book on building shapes in the imagination
video_script.wrong_answer: the square left has an area of four square centimetres
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes the slanting cut as two centimetres, half a side, and gets an area of four square centimetres. The cut is the long side of a corner triangle, so it is longer than two centimetres.
video_script.payoff_line: Both squares have an area of eight square centimetres, half of the starting square

final_answer.value: Both squares have area 8 square cm, half of the starting square
final_answer.spoken: eight square centimetres each, half of the starting square

names.Leeza: engineer quoted on building ideas in the imagination

hold_back: Answer: Both squares have area 8 square cm, half of the starting square
maths_rules: the square has side 4 cm: area 4 x 4 = 16 square cm
each corner triangle has two sides of 2 cm at a right angle: area 2 x 2 / 2 = 2 square cm
four corners: 4 x 2 = 8 square cm, and they fit together into one square
the slanting cut is the long side of a corner triangle, so it is longer than 2 cm
video_script.design: One square on the stage with its midpoints joined; the four corners lift off, turn and fit together; the areas are written one under another.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a square with sides marked 4 cm; the midpoints of the sides are dotted and joined; the four corners lift off

marks.book: the title card and the square appear
marks.cut: the midpoints are joined and the four corners lift off
marks.ask: two question marks appear, one over the square left and one over the square the corners make

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, where Leeza speaks of building ideas in the imagination. Imagine a square with sides of four centimetres.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>Cut off its four corners, each cut joining the midpoints of two neighbouring sides.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the area of the square left, and of the square the four corners make?

beats.on_screen: the square and the lifted corners stay on the board with the question marks underlined

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the four corner triangles turn and meet at one point, fitting together into a new square

marks.turn: the four corners turn so that their right angles meet at one point
marks.fit: the four corners fit together into a new square

narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>Turn the four corners so that their square corners meet at one point.
<bookmark mark='fit'/>They fit together into another square, with no gap and no overlap.

beats.on_screen: Given: square of side 4 cm. Each cut joins the midpoints of two neighbouring sides.

marks.given: the side and the cut are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a square has sides of four centimetres. Each cut joins the midpoints of two neighbouring sides.

beats.on_screen: To find: area of the square left; area of the square made from the 4 corners

marks.find: the two areas to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find two areas. One is the square left, and one is the square made from the corners.

beats.on_screen: Area of the whole square = 4 x 4 = 16 square cm

marks.calc: 4 x 4 = 16 is written under the square

narration: <bookmark mark='calc'/>Step one, find the area of the whole square. Four times four is sixteen square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: One corner: two sides of 2 cm at a right angle. Area = 2 x 2 / 2 = 2 square cm

marks.sides: the two short sides of one corner are marked 2 cm each
marks.calc: 2 x 2 / 2 = 2 is written beside the corner

narration: <bookmark mark='sides'/>Step two, find one corner. Its two short sides are each half of a side of the square, so each is two centimetres.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>The area is two times two, halved, which is two square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Four corners: 4 x 2 = 8 square cm. They fit into one square of area 8 square cm.

marks.calc: 4 x 2 = 8 is written under the new square

narration: <bookmark mark='calc'/>Step three, put the four corners together. Four times two is eight square centimetres, and they fit into one square of that area.

marks.left: 16 - 8 = 8 is written beside the square left

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step four, take the corners away from the whole square. Sixteen minus eight leaves eight square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check the pieces. Eight and eight make sixteen, the area of the whole square.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Both squares have area 8 square cm, half of the starting square
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Both squares have an area of eight square centimetres, half of the starting square.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the cut square
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows side 2 and area 4, struck through; one corner is shown with its slanting side drawn beside the two short sides

marks.doubt: the bubble appears beside the square left
marks.slant: one corner is shown with its slanting side drawn beside a short side, and the slanting side is longer
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the label 8 square cm returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the square left has an area of four square centimetres, because its side is two centimetres.
<bookmark mark='slant'/>The cut slants across a corner. It is the long side of a corner triangle, so it is longer than two centimetres.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The square left is bigger than four. Its area is eight.
